description: Phase 9 U6 polysemy labeled set. Agent-authored, synthetic paraphrase of general legal doctrine; no book or other copyrighted text. Each case is one term in two registered frameworks, the TBox disjointness it asserts, a gold label and the agent's first-pass disposition. Not certified: the FP gate reports provisional until a human certifies it (Phase 9 plan, Open Question 1).

gold_labels.polysemy: related senses across frameworks; a fork with a prime analogate is warranted (accept)
gold_labels.homonymy: unrelated concepts sharing a spelling; no fork (reject with rationale)
gold_labels.univocal: one sense across frameworks; no fork (reject with rationale)

labeling.fp_definition: detector said polysemy and the disposition rejects it with a rationale (KTD9)
labeling.tuning: cases were written before the detector ran on them and are not edited to move the gate

us.common_law: A promise binds only when something is bargained for in return.
The promisee must give a detriment or the promisor receive a benefit in exchange.
A purely gratuitous promise lacks the exchange needed for enforcement.
us.louisiana.civil_code: An obligation needs a lawful reason for which the party binds itself.
A gratuitous promise binds if the giver's motive is lawful and the form is observed.
The reason for obligating oneself need not be an exchange of value.

disposition.rationale: Bargain and civil-law cause both answer why a promise binds; analogous senses, common-law prime.

uk.england.common_law: Something of value in the eye of the law must move from the promisee.
Past acts do not count as the price of a later promise.
A nominal return can support a promise if it is genuinely requested.
us.louisiana.civil_code: A contract is formed by consent, with a lawful motive for the undertaking.
Liberality is a sufficient motive for a donation made in proper form.
The law asks whether the reason for the obligation is lawful, not whether value was exchanged.

disposition.rationale: English price-for-promise and civil-law motive are proportional answers to enforceability.

us.restatement_2d.contracts: A performance or return promise must be sought in exchange for the promise.
The exchange must induce the promise and the promise must induce the exchange.
Adequacy of the exchange is not examined once a bargain exists.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Every obligation rests on a lawful purpose that moved the obligor.
An onerous contract and a gratuitous one can both be valid if their purpose is lawful.
A contract without a lawful purpose is absolutely null.

disposition.rationale: Restatement bargain test and civil-law purpose requirement are analogous validity conditions.

us.ucc: Good faith means honesty in fact and observance of reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing.
Every contract within the commercial code imposes a duty of good faith in its performance.
A merchant who acts honestly but outside fair trade norms may fall short of good faith.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Parties must perform their obligations in good faith throughout the contract.
Bad faith includes a deliberate failure to perform without a lawful excuse.
Good faith governs the formation, performance and termination of conventional obligations.

disposition.rationale: A commercial-standards duty and a general civil-law duty of loyal performance: related senses.

us.common_law: Possession is physical control of a thing with intent to exclude others.
A prior peaceful possessor can recover the thing from a later wrongdoer.
Constructive possession exists when a person can control a thing not held physically.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Possession is the detention or enjoyment of a thing held as owner.
A possessor for one year acquires the right to be maintained in possession.
Possession may be exercised through another who holds the thing for the possessor.

disposition.rationale: Control-with-intent and detention-as-owner are analogous; the civil-law sense adds a possessory right.

us.common_law: Ownership of land is held as an estate measured by its duration.
Different persons may hold present and future estates in the same parcel.
The fee simple is the largest estate a person may hold.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Ownership is the right to use, enjoy and dispose of a thing within legal limits.
The owner holds the thing itself, not an estate in it.
Ownership may be burdened by dismemberments such as usufruct.

disposition.rationale: Estates doctrine versus unitary dominium; analogous senses of the right over property.

us.common_law: Fault in negligence is a failure to use the care a reasonable person would use.
Comparative fault reduces recovery by the plaintiff's share of responsibility.
Fault is measured against an objective standard of conduct.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Every act of a person that causes damage to another obliges the one at fault to repair it.
Fault includes intentional wrongdoing, negligence and imprudence.
The general fault provision is the source of delictual liability.

disposition.rationale: A negligence standard versus the general source of delictual obligation; analogous senses.

us.common_law: A lease conveys a possessory estate in land for a term.
The tenant holds an interest in the land itself during the term.
Covenants in a lease may run with the land to successors.
us.louisiana.civil_code: A lease is a contract by which the lessor binds himself to give the lessee use of a thing for a term.
The lessee's rights are personal rights arising from the contract.
Things movable and immovable alike may be leased.

disposition.rationale: Conveyance of an estate versus a contract for use; analogous senses with the common-law prime.

us.common_law: A trust splits legal title in the trustee from equitable title in the beneficiary.
Equity enforces the trustee's duties for the beneficiary's benefit.
A trust arises from intent, a res and an identified beneficiary.
us.louisiana.civil_code: A trust is a relationship in which property is transferred to a trustee to administer for a beneficiary.
The statutory trust does not divide ownership into legal and equitable shares.
A trust is created by a written instrument in authentic or signed form.

disposition.rationale: Divided-title trust and the statutory civil-law trust: one function, analogous structures.

us.restatement_2d.contracts: A mistake is a belief not in accord with the facts at formation.
A mutual mistake on a basic assumption may make the contract voidable.
The party bearing the risk of the mistake cannot avoid the contract.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Error vitiates consent when it concerns a cause without which the obligation would not have been incurred.
The other party must have known or should have known of that cause.
Error does not vitiate consent when it can be corrected without loss.

disposition.rationale: Basic-assumption mistake and vitiating error answer the same question with different tests.

us.restatement_2d.contracts: An offer manifests willingness to bargain so that assent concludes it.
An offer may be revoked at any time before acceptance unless supported by an option.
A firm offer needs consideration or a statute to stay open.
us.louisiana.civil_code: An offer that specifies a period for acceptance is irrevocable during that time.
An offer without a stated period may be revoked before acceptance is received.
An offer expires if not accepted within a reasonable time.

disposition.rationale: Freely revocable offer versus offer irrevocable by its own terms: analogous senses.

us.ucc: A seller who is a merchant impliedly warrants that goods are merchantable.
An express warranty arises from an affirmation of fact that becomes part of the basis of the bargain.
Warranties may be disclaimed by conspicuous language.
us.louisiana.civil_code: The seller warrants the buyer against redhibitory defects in the thing sold.
A defect that renders the thing useless gives the buyer the right to rescind the sale.
The seller also warrants peaceful possession against eviction.

disposition.rationale: Merchantability warranty and redhibition guarantee: analogous protections, related senses.

us.common_law: A prescriptive easement arises from open, continuous and adverse use for the statutory period.
Permissive use cannot ripen into a prescriptive right.
Prescription creates a servitude-like right, not ownership of the land.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Acquisitive prescription is a mode of acquiring ownership by possession for a period.
Liberative prescription bars an action by inaction for a period.
Prescription runs against all persons unless an exception applies.

disposition.rationale: Use-based easement and the civil-law family of time-based acquisition and loss: analogous senses.

us.common_law: An obligation is a duty one person owes another under a contract.
Breach of an obligation gives the other party a claim for damages.
An obligation may be conditional on an event.
us.louisiana.civil_code: An obligation is a legal relationship whereby an obligor is bound to render a performance in favor of an obligee.
Obligations arise from contracts, from the law and from other declarations of will.
A natural obligation is not enforceable but cannot be reclaimed once performed.

disposition.rationale: A contractual duty versus the juridical bond in general: the civil-law sense is wider, proportionally related.

us.common_law: A contract is a promise or set of promises the law will enforce.
Enforceability depends on offer, acceptance and bargained exchange.
A promise without exchange is not a contract unless reliance supports it.
us.louisiana.civil_code: A contract is an agreement by two or more parties whereby obligations are created, modified or extinguished.
A contract may be onerous or gratuitous.
A contract is formed by the consent of the parties established through offer and acceptance.

disposition.rationale: Enforceable promise versus obligation-creating agreement: analogous senses, prime in common law.

us.ucc: A person has notice of a fact when he has actual knowledge of it or reason to know it.
Notice is given by taking reasonable steps to inform another.
Notice to an organization is effective when it reaches the person handling the transaction.
us.federal.frcp: A complaint need only give fair notice of the claim and its grounds.
Parties must receive notice of a hearing on a motion.
Notice of a dismissal must be filed and served.

disposition.rationale: Knowledge-based notice and procedural notice share the sense of being informed; analogous senses.

us.federal.frcp: A fact is material if it might affect the outcome of the suit.
Summary judgment requires no genuine dispute of material fact.
Immaterial factual disputes do not preclude judgment.
us.restatement_2d.contracts: A breach is material when it deprives the injured party of the benefit reasonably expected.
A material failure of performance suspends the other party's duties.
The extent of compensation available bears on whether a failure is material.

disposition.rationale: Outcome-significance in procedure and in performance: one root sense applied in two frameworks.

us.common_law: The reasonable person is the standard against which conduct is judged in negligence.
Reasonableness is measured by what an ordinarily prudent person would do.
A defendant's subjective good intentions do not make conduct reasonable.
us.ucc: Commercially reasonable conduct follows the practices of the trade.
A disposition of collateral must be commercially reasonable in every aspect.
A reasonable time depends on the nature, purpose and circumstances of the action.

disposition.rationale: Prudent-person and commercial-practice reasonableness: proportional senses of one standard.

us.common_law: A person in tort is a human being who can sue and be sued.
A corporation is treated as a person only by legal fiction for some purposes.
An unborn child is not a person for most common-law claims.
us.louisiana.civil_code: There are two kinds of persons: natural persons and juridical persons.
A juridical person is an entity to which the law attributes personality.
A natural person's personality begins at live birth.

disposition.rationale: Human being with fictional extension versus a two-kind classification: analogous senses.

us.restatement_2d.contracts: A promise that the promisor should expect to induce reliance is binding if injustice can be avoided only by enforcement.
Reliance may be a substitute for bargained exchange.
The remedy may be limited as justice requires.
uk.england.common_law: A promise not to enforce strict rights may prevent their enforcement where the other party relied on it.
The doctrine operates as a shield and not as a sword.
It suspends rather than extinguishes the promisor's rights in many cases.

disposition.rationale: A cause of action and a defensive equity share the reliance sense; analogous senses.

us.common_law: Intestate succession passes a decedent's property to heirs named by statute.
A will displaces intestate succession to the extent of its dispositions.
The personal representative collects and distributes the estate.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Succession is the transmission of the estate of the deceased to successors.
The successors represent the deceased and are bound for the estate's debts within its value.
Forced heirs are entitled to a portion the decedent cannot freely give away.

disposition.rationale: Distribution through a representative versus universal transmission to successors: analogous senses.

us.common_law: Accession gives the owner of a chattel title to improvements added by another's labor.
Where the added value is great, the improver may acquire title subject to compensation.
Accession disputes turn on the relative value of the original and the improvement.
us.louisiana.civil_code: The ownership of a thing includes what it produces and what is united to it.
Fruits belong to the owner of the thing that produces them.
Buildings and plantings become component parts of the land they are attached to.

disposition.rationale: A narrow improvement rule versus a general mode of acquiring fruits and attachments: related senses.

us.federal.frcp: A party who fails to plead or otherwise defend may have its default entered.
A default judgment may be set aside for good cause.
Entry of default precedes a default judgment.
us.ucc: After default, a secured party may take possession of the collateral.
The parties' agreement determines what events constitute default.
A debtor in default may redeem the collateral before its disposition.

disposition.rationale: Failure to answer and failure to pay both name a failure to perform a duty; analogous senses.

us.ucc: Acceptance of goods occurs when the buyer signifies that they are conforming or fails to reject them.
Once goods are accepted, the buyer must pay at the contract rate.
A buyer may revoke acceptance of goods whose nonconformity substantially impairs their value.
us.restatement_2d.contracts: Acceptance of an offer is a manifestation of assent to its terms.
An acceptance must be made in the manner invited by the offer.
A reply that adds conditions is a counter-offer, not an acceptance.

disposition.rationale: Assent to terms and assent to tendered goods: related senses of agreeing to receive.

us.common_law: Expectation damages put the injured party where performance would have put it.
Damages are limited to losses foreseeable at formation.
Punitive damages are generally unavailable for breach of contract.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Damages are measured by the loss sustained and the profit of which the obligee was deprived.
An obligor in good faith is liable only for damages foreseeable at the time of the contract.
Damages for nonpecuniary loss may be recovered when the contract was meant to gratify a nonpecuniary interest.

disposition.rationale: Expectation measure and loss-plus-lost-profit measure: close but framework-scoped senses.

cases.note: Close senses; the TBox records a conflict on non-pecuniary loss.

us.common_law: Each spouse owns what he or she earns, subject to equitable division at divorce.
Courts divide marital property according to fairness factors.
Title alone does not decide distribution on divorce.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Property acquired during the community regime by either spouse is community property.
Each spouse owns a present undivided one-half interest in community property.
Separate property includes things acquired before marriage or by inheritance.

disposition.rationale: Separate-title equitable distribution and community ownership: analogous senses.

us.common_law: An easement appurtenant benefits a dominant parcel.
Servitudes include easements, profits and covenants running with land.
An easement may be created by express grant or by necessity.
us.louisiana.civil_code: A predial servitude is a charge on a servient estate for the benefit of a dominant estate.
Personal servitudes include usufruct, habitation and rights of use.
Servitudes are established by title, by destination of the owner or by prescription.

disposition.rationale: Anglo-American servitudes and civil-law predial and personal servitudes are analogous senses.

cases.note: No TBox seed: Rule 1 cannot fire; expected false negative.

us.common_law: A minor may disaffirm most contracts made before majority.
Contracts for necessaries bind a minor to pay reasonable value.
Mental incapacity makes a contract voidable.
us.louisiana.civil_code: All persons have capacity to contract except unemancipated minors, interdicts and persons deprived of reason.
A contract made by a person without capacity is relatively null.
Emancipation confers capacity in whole or in part.

disposition.rationale: Disaffirmance doctrine and statutory incapacity with relative nullity: analogous senses.

cases.note: No TBox seed: expected false negative.

us.ucc: A modification of a sales contract needs no consideration to bind.
A signed firm offer by a merchant is irrevocable without consideration.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Consent with a lawful motive suffices to form a contract.
A donation inter vivos binds if made in authentic form.

disposition.rationale: Commercial dispensations from consideration and civil-law cause relate to the same validity question.

cases.note: Two axioms per framework: Rule 2 holds the evidence insufficient.

us.federal.frcp: A final judgment on the merits bars a later suit on the same claim.
Claim preclusion acts as a bar to relitigation.
A defense of bar must be raised in the answer.
us.common_law: Admission to the bar requires passing the licensing examination.
Members of the bar owe duties of candor to the court.
The bar disciplines lawyers who violate ethical rules.

disposition.rationale: Preclusion and the legal profession share only a spelling; not a fork.

us.ucc: A security interest is a right in personal property that secures payment.
A security interest attaches when value is given and the debtor has rights in the collateral.
Perfection of a security interest gives priority over later creditors.
us.common_law: Prejudgment interest compensates for the time value of money withheld.
Interest accrues at the legal rate absent a contractual rate.
Usury law caps the rate of interest a lender may charge.

disposition.rationale: A property right in collateral versus a charge for the use of money; homonyms.

us.restatement_2d.contracts: A party executes a written contract by signing and delivering it.
An executed contract is one fully performed on both sides.
Execution of a deed requires the grantor's signature.
us.federal.frcp: A money judgment is enforced by a writ of execution.
Execution proceedings follow the law of the state where the court sits.
Property levied on in execution may be sold to satisfy the judgment.

disposition.rationale: Signing or performing a contract versus enforcing a judgment; homonyms.

us.federal.frcp: The plaintiff must serve the summons and complaint on each defendant.
Service may be made by delivering a copy to the individual personally.
Later papers are served on the party's attorney.
us.common_law: A convicted defendant must serve the sentence imposed by the court.
Time served in pretrial custody is credited against the sentence.
A prisoner may serve concurrent terms.

disposition.rationale: Delivering process versus undergoing punishment; unrelated legal concepts.

us.louisiana.civil_code: Cause is the reason why a party obligates himself.
An obligation cannot exist without a lawful cause.
The cause need not be expressed in the contract.
us.federal.frcp: A deadline may be extended for good cause.
A scheduling order may be modified only for good cause and with the judge's consent.
Good cause requires diligence by the party seeking relief.

disposition.rationale: A validity element of obligations versus a showing for procedural relief; homonyms.

us.federal.fre: The court may exclude relevant evidence if its probative value is substantially outweighed by unfair prejudice.
Judges weigh the danger of confusing the issues against probative value.
Expert testimony is admitted after the court considers the reliability of the method.
us.common_law: A promise binds only when something is bargained for in return.
Past performance cannot serve as the price of a new promise.
Courts do not inquire into the adequacy of what was exchanged.

disposition.rationale: Judicial weighing and bargained-for exchange share only the word; not a fork.

us.federal.fre: Relevant evidence is evidence that makes a fact of consequence more or less probable.
The court weighs probative value against the risk of misleading the jury.
Needless presentation of cumulative evidence may be excluded.
us.restatement_2d.contracts: A performance or return promise must be bargained for.
The exchange must induce the promise.
A gift promise is unenforceable without a substitute such as reliance.

disposition.rationale: Evidentiary weighing versus the bargain element; homonyms.

us.federal.frcp: The judge's charge instructs the jury on the law it must apply.
A party must object to the charge before the jury retires.
An erroneous charge may require a new trial.
us.ucc: A bank may charge a customer's account for a properly payable item.
An item is properly payable if authorized by the customer.
A bank that charges an account wrongly must recredit it.

disposition.rationale: Jury instructions versus debiting an account; homonyms.

us.ucc: A draft is an order by the drawer to the drawee to pay money.
A check is a draft drawn on a bank and payable on demand.
The drawee is not liable on a draft until it accepts.
us.restatement_2d.contracts: A preliminary draft of an agreement may show the parties did not intend to be bound yet.
Exchanging drafts can be evidence of ongoing negotiation.
A party may intend to be bound only when a final draft is signed.

disposition.rationale: A payment order versus a version of a document; homonyms.

us.federal.frcp: Prejudgment attachment seizes property to secure a possible judgment.
State law governs the availability of attachment at the start of an action.
Attachment requires notice and an opportunity to be heard in most cases.
us.ucc: A security interest attaches when it becomes enforceable against the debtor.
Attachment requires value, rights in the collateral and an authenticated agreement.
Attachment is distinct from perfection against third parties.

disposition.rationale: A judicial seizure remedy versus enforceability of a security interest; homonyms.

us.louisiana.civil_code: Compensation extinguishes two obligations owed reciprocally when both are liquidated and due.
Compensation takes place by operation of law.
Compensation cannot be invoked against a claim for return of a deposit.
us.common_law: Workers receive compensation for injuries arising out of employment.
Just compensation is owed when the government takes property.
Compensatory damages restore the plaintiff's loss.

disposition.rationale: Mutual extinguishment of debts versus payment for loss; unrelated concepts.

us.ucc: A note is a promise to pay a sum of money signed by the maker.
A negotiable note is payable to bearer or to order.
A holder in due course takes a note free of most defenses.
us.federal.frcp: Advisory committee notes explain the purpose of an amendment to the rules.
Courts consult the notes when a rule is ambiguous.
The notes are not binding but are persuasive.

disposition.rationale: A negotiable promise to pay versus explanatory commentary; homonyms.

us.federal.frcp: Service of process gives the court personal jurisdiction over the defendant.
A defendant may waive formal service.
Proof of service must be filed with the court.
us.common_law: A contract for personal services cannot be specifically enforced against the worker.
An employer is liable for torts committed in the course of service.
Services rendered without a promise of payment may support restitution.

disposition.rationale: Delivering process versus labor performed for another; homonyms.

us.ucc: A negotiable instrument is an unconditional promise or order to pay a fixed amount.
An instrument must be payable on demand or at a definite time.
Transfer of an instrument vests the transferor's right to enforce it.
us.federal.fre: A deadly instrument may be offered as real evidence after authentication.
A physical instrument used in the incident must be shown to be what the proponent claims.
Chain of custody supports the authentication of an instrument seized by police.

disposition.rationale: A payment writing versus a physical object in evidence; homonyms.

us.restatement_2d.contracts: A party to a contract is bound by the promises it makes.
A third party beneficiary may enforce a promise made for its benefit.
The parties may agree to modify their contract.
us.federal.frcp: A party may join any claim it has against an opposing party.
A person whose absence prevents complete relief must be joined as a party.
A party may amend its pleading once as a matter of course.

disposition.rationale: Labeled homonymy on the whitelist's reading: a contracting party and a litigant are distinct roles.

cases.note: Debatable label (the whitelist treats party as a homonym); Rule 4 routes it to the LLM.

us.common_law: A sentence is the punishment a court imposes on a convicted defendant.
A sentence may be suspended on conditions.
Consecutive sentences run one after another.
us.federal.frcp: A pleading must state each claim in numbered paragraphs, each limited to a single set of circumstances.
Each averment should be simple, concise and direct.
A court may strike a redundant sentence from a pleading.

disposition.rationale: Criminal punishment versus a unit of text in a pleading; homonyms.

us.ucc: Title to goods passes when the seller completes delivery unless otherwise agreed.
A person with voidable title can transfer good title to a good faith purchaser.
Title cannot pass before the goods are identified to the contract.
us.federal.frcp: The title of a pleading names the court and the parties.
The complaint's title must include the names of all parties.
Captions and titles do not control the substance of a pleading.

disposition.rationale: Ownership of goods versus a document heading; homonyms.

us.federal.frcp: A request for a court order must be made by motion.
A motion must state its grounds with particularity.
A motion to dismiss tests the legal sufficiency of the complaint.
us.common_law: A moving vehicle's motion creates foreseeable risks to pedestrians.
Res ipsa loquitur may apply when an object in motion strikes the plaintiff.
The defendant set the object in motion and is responsible for its path.

disposition.rationale: A procedural request versus physical movement; homonyms.

cases.note: No TBox seed: Rule 1 does not fire.

us.common_law: A criminal charge accuses a person of an offense.
The prosecution bears the burden of proving every element of the charge.
us.ucc: A collecting bank may charge back a provisional credit.
The right to charge back ends when the settlement becomes final.

disposition.rationale: An accusation versus reversing a credit; homonyms.

cases.note: Two axioms per framework: Rule 2 holds the evidence insufficient.

us.common_law: A promise binds only when something is bargained for in return.
Past performance does not support a later promise.
Courts do not weigh the adequacy of the exchange.
uk.england.common_law: Consideration must move from the promisee.
Past consideration is no consideration.
Consideration must be sufficient but need not be adequate.

disposition.rationale: Both frameworks share the bargain sense; no fork.

us.restatement_2d.contracts: A performance or return promise must be bargained for.
The exchange must induce the promise.
Nominal consideration does not support an option unless it is recited in a signed writing.
us.ucc: A sales contract requires the usual exchange of goods for a price.
A modification needs no new consideration, but the original contract still rests on exchange.
The price may be payable in money or otherwise.

disposition.rationale: The commercial code assumes the same bargain sense of consideration; no fork.

us.common_law: Conversion is an intentional exercise of dominion over another's chattel.
The converter is liable for the full value of the chattel.
A good faith purchaser from a thief can still be liable for conversion.
us.ucc: An instrument is converted when it is taken by transfer from a person not entitled to enforce it.
The law of conversion of personal property applies to instruments.
A bank that pays on a forged indorsement may be liable in conversion.

disposition.rationale: The commercial code applies the common-law tort to instruments; one sense.

us.ucc: Tender of delivery requires the seller to put conforming goods at the buyer's disposition.
Tender must be at a reasonable hour and the goods kept available for a reasonable time.
The buyer's duty to pay is conditioned on the seller's tender.
us.common_law: Tender is an unconditional offer to perform an obligation.
A valid tender of payment stops the running of interest.
A refused tender excuses the tendering party from further performance.

disposition.rationale: An offer of performance in both frameworks; one sense.

us.federal.frcp: A court must have subject-matter jurisdiction to decide a case.
Lack of personal jurisdiction is waived if not timely raised.
A court may examine its own jurisdiction at any time.
uk.england.common_law: A court has jurisdiction when the law confers on it power to decide the dispute.
Jurisdiction over a defendant may rest on presence within the territory.
A judgment given without jurisdiction is a nullity.

disposition.rationale: Power to adjudicate in both frameworks; univocal.

us.common_law: A minor is a person under the age of majority.
The age of majority is set by statute, usually eighteen.
A minor may sue through a guardian or next friend.
us.louisiana.civil_code: A minor is a person who has not reached the age of eighteen years.
A minor may be emancipated by judgment or by marriage.
Parents administer the property of their minor children.

disposition.rationale: A person under the age of majority in both frameworks; univocal.

us.common_law: Fraud is a knowing misrepresentation of a material fact intended to induce reliance.
The victim must justifiably rely on the misrepresentation.
A contract induced by fraud is voidable.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Fraud is a misrepresentation or suppression of the truth made to obtain an unjust advantage.
Fraud vitiates consent when it concerns a circumstance that substantially influenced it.
Fraud may result from silence when there is a duty to speak.

disposition.rationale: Deceit inducing consent in both frameworks; univocal.

us.restatement_2d.contracts: Duress by improper threat that leaves no reasonable alternative makes a contract voidable.
A threat of crime or tort is improper.
Physical compulsion prevents assent altogether.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Consent is vitiated when obtained by duress that would cause a reasonable fear of unjust injury.
Age, health and personality of the victim are considered.
A threat to do a lawful act is not duress.

disposition.rationale: Coerced consent in both frameworks; univocal.

us.restatement_2d.contracts: A breach occurs when performance is due and not rendered.
Every breach gives rise to a claim for damages.
A total breach discharges the injured party's remaining duties.
us.louisiana.civil_code: An obligor is liable for failure to perform an obligation.
Failure to perform may consist of nonperformance, defective performance or delay.
The obligee may demand dissolution when the obligor fails to perform.

disposition.rationale: Failure to render due performance in both frameworks; univocal.

us.restatement_2d.contracts: An assignment transfers a contractual right to the assignee.
Rights may be assigned unless assignment materially changes the obligor's duty.
The obligor may raise against the assignee defenses it had against the assignor.
us.louisiana.civil_code: A right may be assigned to a third person unless it is strictly personal.
The assignee acquires the right with its accessories.
The assignment is effective against the debtor once the debtor has notice of it.

disposition.rationale: Transfer of a right to an assignee in both frameworks; univocal.

us.restatement_2d.contracts: A novation substitutes a new obligation and discharges the original one.
A novation may substitute a new obligor with the obligee's assent.
Intent to discharge the old duty is required.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Novation is the extinguishment of an existing obligation by the substitution of a new one.
The intent to novate may not be presumed.
Substitution of a new obligor requires the obligee's consent.

disposition.rationale: Extinguishment by substitution in both frameworks; univocal.

us.common_law: A mortgage is a security interest in real property for a debt.
On default, the mortgagee may foreclose and sell the property.
The mortgagor keeps possession until foreclosure.
us.louisiana.civil_code: A mortgage is a nonpossessory right created over property to secure an obligation.
The mortgagee may cause the property to be seized and sold on default.
A mortgage follows the property into the hands of a third possessor.

disposition.rationale: A nonpossessory security over property in both frameworks; univocal.

us.federal.fre: Every person is competent to be a witness unless a rule provides otherwise.
A witness may testify only to matters within personal knowledge.
A witness must give an oath or affirmation to testify truthfully.
uk.england.common_law: A witness is a person who gives evidence of facts before a court.
A witness may be compelled to attend by a summons.
A witness may be cross-examined by the opposing party.

disposition.rationale: One who testifies in both frameworks; univocal.

us.federal.fre: A qualified expert may give an opinion if it will help the trier of fact.
The opinion must rest on sufficient facts and reliable methods.
An expert may base an opinion on facts not admissible in evidence.
uk.england.common_law: An expert gives opinion evidence on matters outside the court's knowledge.
An expert's duty is to the court, overriding any duty to the party paying.
An expert must state the facts and assumptions on which the opinion rests.

disposition.rationale: An opinion-giving witness in both frameworks; univocal.

us.federal.fre: Evidence is relevant if it makes a fact of consequence more or less probable.
Irrelevant evidence is not admissible.
Relevance is a low threshold.
uk.england.common_law: Evidence is relevant if it is logically probative of a fact in issue.
Only relevant evidence is admissible.
Relevance is a matter of logic and common sense.

disposition.rationale: Logical tendency to prove a fact in both frameworks; univocal.

us.federal.fre: A presumption shifts the burden of producing evidence to the opposing party.
The burden of persuasion stays with the party who bore it originally.
The party asserting a claim generally bears the burden of proving it.
us.louisiana.civil_code: A party who demands performance of an obligation must prove its existence.
A party who asserts that an obligation is null must prove the facts of nullity.
The burden of proof rests on the party asserting the fact.

disposition.rationale: Allocation of the duty to prove in both frameworks; univocal.

us.federal.frcp: The plaintiff commences an action by filing a complaint.
The plaintiff must serve each defendant.
A plaintiff may voluntarily dismiss before an answer is served.
us.common_law: The plaintiff must prove every element of the tort.
A plaintiff who consents to a risk may be barred from recovery.
The plaintiff's damages must be proved with reasonable certainty.

disposition.rationale: The party who brings suit in both frameworks; univocal.

us.federal.frcp: A judgment is any order from which an appeal lies.
A judgment must be set out in a separate document.
A court may relieve a party from a final judgment for mistake.
uk.england.common_law: A judgment is the court's final decision determining the rights of the parties.
A judgment may be enforced by the successful party.
A judgment binds the parties on the issues decided.

disposition.rationale: The court's decision of the parties' rights in both frameworks; univocal.

us.federal.frcp: A party may appeal a final judgment to the court of appeals.
The notice of appeal must be filed within the time allowed.
Interlocutory orders are generally not appealable.
us.louisiana.civil_code: An appeal is the exercise of the right of a party to have a judgment revised by a higher court.
An appeal may be devolutive or suspensive.
A suspensive appeal requires security.

disposition.rationale: Review by a higher court in both frameworks; univocal.

us.ucc: Goods are things movable at the time of identification to the contract.
Money in which the price is payable is not goods.
Growing crops and unborn animals can be goods.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Corporeal movables are things that can be moved from one place to another.
A sale of corporeal movables passes ownership on agreement.
Standing timber may be treated as a movable by anticipation.

disposition.rationale: Movable things in both frameworks; univocal.

us.ucc: The price may be fixed later by the parties or a third person.
If the price is not settled, it is a reasonable price at delivery.
Payment of the price is due at the time and place the buyer receives the goods.
us.louisiana.civil_code: The price must be fixed by the parties in a sum either certain or determinable.
The price must not be out of all proportion to the value of the thing.
The buyer is bound to pay the price at the time and place stipulated.

disposition.rationale: The money paid for the thing sold in both frameworks; univocal.

us.ucc: The seller must transfer and deliver the goods in accordance with the contract.
Unless otherwise agreed, the place for delivery is the seller's place of business.
Delivery in installments is permitted only if agreed.
us.louisiana.civil_code: Delivery of a movable takes place by handing it over to the buyer.
The seller must deliver the thing in the condition it was in at the time of sale.
Delivery of an immovable is deemed to take place on execution of the act of sale.

disposition.rationale: Handing over the thing sold in both frameworks; univocal.

us.common_law: A waiver is the intentional relinquishment of a known right.
Waiver may be express or implied from conduct.
A waiver of a condition may be retracted unless the other party relied on it.
us.ucc: A party who waives an executory portion may retract the waiver by reasonable notice.
A retraction is ineffective if it would be unjust because of a material change of position.
An attempted modification that fails may still operate as a waiver.

disposition.rationale: Relinquishment of a known right in both frameworks; univocal.

us.common_law: An agent acts on behalf of a principal and subject to the principal's control.
An agent owes the principal duties of loyalty and obedience.
A principal is bound by an agent's acts within actual or apparent authority.
us.louisiana.civil_code: A mandatary is authorized by a principal to transact affairs for the principal.
The mandatary must act prudently and in good faith for the principal.
The principal is bound by contracts the mandatary makes within the authority given.

disposition.rationale: One who acts for a principal in both frameworks; univocal.

us.common_law: A will disposes of property at death and is revocable during life.
A will must be signed and attested by witnesses.
A later will revokes an earlier inconsistent one.
us.louisiana.civil_code: A testament disposes of property at death and may be revoked at any time.
An olographic testament must be entirely written, dated and signed by the testator.
A notarial testament is executed before a notary and two witnesses.

disposition.rationale: A revocable disposition at death in both frameworks; univocal.

us.common_law: Co-owners may seek partition of land they hold together.
Partition in kind is preferred where practicable.
A court may order partition by sale when division is impractical.
us.louisiana.civil_code: No one may be compelled to hold a thing in indivision with another.
Partition may be made by agreement or by judgment.
A thing that cannot be divided conveniently is partitioned by licitation.

disposition.rationale: Ending co-ownership by division or sale in both frameworks; univocal.

us.federal.frcp: A pleading must demand the relief sought.
A final judgment should grant the relief to which each party is entitled.
Relief in the alternative may be demanded.
uk.england.common_law: A claim form must state the remedy the claimant seeks.
The court may grant any remedy to which the claimant is entitled.
Equitable remedies are discretionary.

disposition.rationale: The remedy a party seeks from the court in both frameworks; univocal.

us.common_law: Domicile is the place where a person resides with intent to remain indefinitely.
A person has only one domicile at a time.
A domicile continues until a new one is acquired.
us.louisiana.civil_code: The domicile of a natural person is the place of habitual residence.
A person may change domicile by moving with the intent to make the new residence habitual.
Proof of intent to change domicile depends on the circumstances.

disposition.rationale: Residence with intent in both frameworks; the TBox seed over-asserts a conflict.

us.common_law: Negligence requires a duty, breach, causation and damage.
The standard of care is that of a reasonably prudent person.
Foreseeability limits the scope of liability.
uk.england.common_law: Negligence requires a duty of care, breach, causation and loss that is not too remote.
The standard of care is that of the reasonable person in the defendant's position.
Liability extends to reasonably foreseeable kinds of harm.

disposition.rationale: The same tort elements in both frameworks; the TBox seed over-asserts a conflict.

cases.note: Over-asserted TBox seed; a terms-of-art term (0.75 threshold).

us.restatement_2d.contracts: A party to a contract is a person who makes or receives a promise in it.
The parties' intent governs interpretation.
A party may assign its rights.
us.federal.frcp: A party is a person named in the action as plaintiff or defendant.
A party may serve interrogatories on another party.
Each party bears its own costs unless the court orders otherwise.

disposition.rationale: Read as one sense (a participant in a legal transaction or proceeding); no TBox conflict.

cases.note: Contrast with h-party-r2-frcp-seed: the same term labeled from the univocal reading.

us.ucc: Good faith means honesty in fact and the observance of reasonable commercial standards.
Every contract imposes an obligation of good faith in performance.
Good faith cannot be disclaimed by agreement.
us.restatement_2d.contracts: Every contract imposes a duty of good faith and fair dealing in its performance.
Bad faith includes evasion of the spirit of the bargain.
Good faith excludes conduct that violates community standards of decency.

disposition.rationale: The same performance duty in both US frameworks; univocal.

us.restatement_2d.contracts: A misrepresentation is material if it would likely induce a reasonable person to assent.
A material misrepresentation can make a contract voidable.
us.ucc: Additional terms that materially alter an offer do not become part of the contract.
A clause causing surprise or hardship materially alters the contract.

disposition.rationale: A significance threshold in both frameworks; univocal.

us.ucc: A seller is a person who sells or contracts to sell goods.
The seller must tender conforming goods.
A seller may cure a nonconforming tender within the contract time.
us.louisiana.civil_code: The seller is bound to deliver the thing sold and to warrant it.
The seller must clearly declare the extent of his obligations.
Any doubt about the seller's obligations is interpreted in favor of the buyer.

disposition.rationale: The party who sells in both frameworks; univocal.

uk.england.common_law: An appeal lies from the High Court to the Court of Appeal with permission.
The appeal court will allow an appeal where the decision was wrong.
Permission to appeal is granted where there is a real prospect of success.
us.federal.frcp: A notice of appeal designates the judgment appealed from.
An appeal as of right is taken by filing a notice with the district clerk.
The time to appeal runs from entry of the judgment.

disposition.rationale: Review by a higher court in both frameworks; the TBox seed over-asserts a conflict.
